access_continuity_justification: Not yet met: only one person can merge and release. Mitigations are documented (Apache-2.0 allows forking; the release pipeline needs no stored secrets; release steps are documented), and adding a co-maintainer is the planned remedy. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The terminal interface never uses color as the only carrier of information (states also have text or symbols), honors NO_COLOR, is fully keyboard-driven, and works in a plain 80x24 terminal.
achieve_passing_justification: The project has the passing badge (100%).
assurance_case_justification: docs/assurance-case.md: threat model, trust boundaries, secure design principles applied and common weaknesses countered, each with evidence, plus residual risks. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
automated_integration_testing_justificat: Every push and pull request runs the full test suite in GitHub Actions, which reports success or failure per check.
build_common_tools_justification: The standard Go toolchain (go build, go test).
build_floss_tools_justification: Built and tested only with FLOSS tools: Go, golangci-lint, govulncheck, socat.
build_justification: Standard Go build: go build ./cmd/modtop (documented in the README); CI builds every change. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
build_non_recursive_justification: The Go toolchain builds from the full package dependency graph; there is no recursive build system.
build_preserve_debug_justification: A plain go build keeps the debugging information; only the published release binaries are stripped (-s -w), on purpose and visibly in the release workflow.
build_repeatable_justification: Release builds are bit-for-bit reproducible: rebuilding v0.1.1 and v0.1.2 from the tagged source with the documented commands reproduces the published SHA256SUMS (verified). https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#reproducing-a-release
build_standard_variables_justification: The build is the plain Go toolchain (go build), which honors the standard Go environment variables (GOFLAGS, GOOS, GOARCH, GOARM and the CGO_* variables); no build script overrides them. No C compiler is used (CGO_ENABLED=0).
bus_factor_justification: The bus factor is 1 (single maintainer), as stated in GOVERNANCE.md. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
code_of_conduct_justification: Contributor Covenant 2.1, in the standard location. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
coding_standards_enforced_justification: gofmt and golangci-lint run in CI as required checks; merges are blocked on any finding.
coding_standards_justification: Effective Go and the Go Code Review Comments, gofmt and the repository's golangci-lint configuration. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-style
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md describes the contribution process: proposals, checks to run, rules and squash-merged pull requests. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md lists the requirements for acceptable contributions (tests required, read-only rule, English, Conventional Commits, pinned CI actions); GOVERNANCE.md lists the feature acceptance criteria. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
crypto_call_justification: modtop implements and calls no cryptographic functions.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: modtop processes no credentials or private keys.
crypto_pfs_justification: modtop has no key agreement protocol.
crypto_published_justification: modtop implements no cryptography; Modbus TCP and RTU have no cryptographic layer.
crypto_random_justification: modtop generates no cryptographic keys or nonces.
crypto_used_network_justification: modtop speaks Modbus TCP and Modbus RTU, which have no encryption or authentication. Secure Modbus (Modbus/TCP over TLS) is not supported; the README documents using an SSH tunnel for remote access.
dco_justification: Contributions require a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off (git commit -s); a required CI check fails pull requests with unsigned commits. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin
delivery_mitm_justification: Source and binaries are delivered over HTTPS from GitHub; releases include SHA256SUMS and build provenance attestations (Sigstore). https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/releases
delivery_unsigned_justification: Checksums are only published over HTTPS (GitHub releases), together with a signed provenance attestation.
dependency_monitoring_justification: govulncheck runs on every change; GitHub Dependabot alerts and security updates are enabled, and Dependabot proposes updates weekly.
description_good_justification: The README starts by stating what modtop does: an interactive terminal tool to see and understand what a Modbus device is saying, live, including over SSH on headless field gateways. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/README.md
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests are searchable, addressable by URL and open to anyone. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/issues
documentation_achievements_justification: The README front page shows and links the OpenSSF Best Practices badge. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/README.md
documentation_architecture_justification: docs/architecture.md describes the packages, the dependency rule, the data flow, concurrency and the properties the design keeps. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/docs/architecture.md
documentation_basics_justification: The README covers installation, the three usage modes, options, keys, exit codes, safety and troubleshooting; docs/addressing.md explains Modbus addressing. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/README.md
documentation_current_justification: The documentation is reviewed with each change; pull requests that change behavior update the README, docs and CHANGELOG in the same pull request.
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface is the command line and the keyboard: options, keys and exit codes are documented in the README and printed by modtop --help. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/README.md#usage
documentation_quick_start_justification: The README starts with a three-command quick start. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/README.md#quick-start
documentation_roadmap_justification: ROADMAP.md covers October 2026 to October 2027, including what is not planned. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_security_justification: SECURITY.md states what users can and cannot expect; docs/assurance-case.md argues why. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-model-what-you-can-and-cannot-expect
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The Go runtime always checks bounds, nil dereferences and type assertions; the test suite also runs with the race detector, which instruments memory accesses (the fuzzers run without it).
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Findings are fixed promptly; for example, a data race found by the race detector during development was fixed before merge (pull request #7).
dynamic_analysis_justification: Native Go fuzzing of the TCP and RTU response parsers runs in CI, and the whole test suite runs with the race detector.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: modtop is written in Go, a memory-safe language, and uses neither cgo nor the unsafe package.
english_justification: All documentation, code, messages and discussion are in English.
enhancement_responses_justification: No external enhancement request has been filed yet; requests are answered per GOVERNANCE.md, which states the acceptance criteria.
external_dependencies_justification: go.mod and go.sum list every dependency with its version and checksum. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/go.mod
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md documents how decisions are made (a single maintainer decides, in public issues and pull requests, against written acceptance criteria). https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#decision-making
hardening_justification: Go provides mandatory bounds and nil checks and a memory-safe runtime; binaries are static with no cgo; the container image is an empty (scratch) base running as a non-root user.
implement_secure_design_justification: Fail-safe defaults, least privilege, complete mediation, economy of mechanism and defense in depth are applied as described in the assurance case. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
input_validation_justification: All command-line input is checked against allowlists and ranges before any connection (including that a serial path is a serial device), and every field of every device response is validated before use; a response is only accepted for the request it answers.
installation_common_justification: Install with go install github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/cmd/modtop@latest (uninstall by deleting the binary), as a container image from ghcr.io, or by downloading the static binary. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/README.md#installation
installation_development_quick_justifica: Clone and run go test ./...: Go modules fetch every dependency; socat (optional, for the RTU tests) comes from the system package manager. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#development-setup
installation_standard_variables_justific: go install honors GOBIN and GOPATH; the release binary is a single file the user places where they choose.
interact_justification: The README explains how to obtain modtop (releases page), how to report issues and how to contribute (CONTRIBUTING.md, pull requests). https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/README.md
interfaces_current_justification: staticcheck (through golangci-lint) reports uses of deprecated APIs, and CI blocks them.
internationalization_justification: All interface text is English and is not externalized for translation; this is a deliberate project decision for a small diagnostic tool.
know_common_errors_justification: Common errors are countered: memory safety (Go, no cgo, no unsafe); malformed input (response parsers are fuzzed in CI and must never panic); integer and length errors (sizes validated before use); concurrency errors (race detector in CI); dependency vulnerabilities (govulncheck); secrets (secret scanning with push protection); supply chain (SHA-pinned CI actions, checksums and provenance attestations).
know_secure_design_justification: The design applies: fail-safe defaults and least privilege (read-only by absence of write code, enforced by a CI guard; a serial port in use is refused unless explicitly forced); complete mediation and input validation (all arguments validated before any connection; every response checked for size, CRC, IDs and function); economy of mechanism (small, dependency-light code); defense in depth for the serial port (/proc scan, UUCP locks, flock, TIOCEXCL).
license_location_justification: The license is in the LICENSE file at the repository root. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/LICENSE
maintained_justification: The project is actively maintained; see the commit and release history. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/commits/main
maintenance_or_update_justification: Upgrading is replacing a single static binary (or image tag). The command line, exit codes and safety behavior are contracts that only change through a documented deprecation process. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#deprecation
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The repository holds no credentials; GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled.
regression_tests_added50_justification: Every bug fixed so far came with a regression test: the RTU late-answer and TCP partial-frame fixes (#17) with TestRTULateResponseNotTakenForNext and TestTCPPartialFrameTimeoutResyncs, each confirmed to fail on the previous code; the command-line fixes (#18) with a test per case; and the data race fixed in #7 is exercised under the race detector in CI.
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog) summarizes each release; the release page carries the same notes. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability has been fixed in any release; the changelog has a Security section for future fixes.
repo_interim_justification: Interim work between releases is public: changes are pull requests merged into main, visible before and after release. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/pulls?q=is%3Apr
repo_track_justification: Git records every change with author and date. Since the initial commit, every change has gone through a pull request with required CI checks.
report_archive_justification: The GitHub issue tracker keeps a public, searchable archive of reports and responses. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/issues?q=is%3Aissue
report_process_justification: Bugs are reported through GitHub issues, with a bug report form. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/issues/new/choose
report_responses_justification: No bug report has been filed on the issue tracker yet. Defects found by an external review in October 2026 were reproduced, fixed with regression tests and released the same day (v0.1.2). https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/releases/tag/v0.1.2
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md lists the roles (maintainer, release manager, security responder, code of conduct enforcement), their tasks and who holds each. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
signed_releases_justification: Release binaries and the container image carry Sigstore build provenance attestations (keyless, so no private key is stored anywhere), version tags are signed with an SSH key whose public half is in the repository, and the README explains how to verify both. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/README.md#verifying-a-release
sites_https_justification: The project site, repository and downloads are on GitHub over HTTPS: https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites are GitHub and bestpractices.dev; the project stores no passwords itself.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: gosec looks for common vulnerability patterns; govulncheck checks dependencies and the standard library against the Go vulnerability database.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: All findings are fixed before merge; CI blocks merges with findings.
static_analysis_justification: golangci-lint (staticcheck, govet, errcheck, gosec, errorlint and others) and govulncheck run on every push and pull request. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs on every push and pull request.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs lint, vet, race-enabled tests, fuzzing, a vulnerability check and builds on every push and pull request. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_invocation_justification: go test ./... (standard Go invocation; documented in CONTRIBUTING.md).
test_justification: An automated test suite (go test) covers every package, including golden-file tests of the screen and a Modbus simulator for TCP and RTU. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_most_justification: Statement coverage is 88% across all packages; per product package it is between 77% and 96% (go test -cover).
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md: every change comes with tests in the same pull request, and bug fixes come with a regression test. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md: every change comes with tests in the same pull request. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#rules
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Statement coverage across all packages is 88% (go test -coverpkg=./...); CI fails below 80%.
tests_are_added_justification: Every merged pull request that adds or fixes behavior adds tests (e.g. #1 to #7, #17, #18). https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged
tests_documented_added_justification: The test policy is in CONTRIBUTING.md and in the pull request template checklist. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
updateable_reused_components_justificati: All reused components are Go modules managed by go.mod; there are no vendored or forked copies.
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning, as stated in CHANGELOG.md.
version_tags_justification: Each release is identified by an annotated git tag (v0.1.0, v0.1.1, v0.1.2). https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/tags
version_tags_signed_justification: Version tags are signed from v0.1.1 on (the first release, v0.1.0, predates this); verify with git tag -v and .github/allowed_signers. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/tags
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique version (first release: v0.1.0). https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/releases
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: There are no known critical vulnerabilities.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no publicly known vulnerabilities; govulncheck runs on every change.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability has been reported or resolved; SECURITY.md commits to crediting reporters.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports go through GitHub private vulnerability reporting, which is enabled. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md describes how to report vulnerabilities. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received; SECURITY.md commits to an acknowledgement within 5 business days.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md documents how reports are handled: acknowledgement, assessment, private fix, advisory and credit. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-we-handle-a-report
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any vet or lint finding; the code base has zero findings.
warnings_justification: go vet and golangci-lint (standard linters plus gosec and errorlint) run in CI. https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/modtop/blob/main/.golangci.yml
warnings_strict_justification: golangci-lint runs the standard set plus gosec and errorlint; the only exclusion (gosec G115, intentional integer truncation in the binary protocol codec) is documented in .golangci.yml.
